text:
In CPU intensive games, the two main factors that make the RTX 4060 perform better than the Intel Arc B580 are:

1. Larger L2 Cache:

When there is more L2 cache, there is faster access to data, and the latency or delay between the processor and the GPU is reduced. This is crucial in CPU intensive games, as the CPU needs to access more data, and a larger cache can speed up these processes.

2. Lower Bandwidth and Reduced CPU Load:

When the GPU has lower bandwidth, the CPU has less strain to handle. In this case, the GPU requires less bandwidth, allowing the CPU to access data more quickly. This helps reduce the CPU bottleneck and results in better performance in games that are more dependent on the CPU.

As a result, these two factors make the RTX 4060 perform better in CPU intensive games compared to the Intel Arc B580, because the lower bandwidth and larger cache help the CPU process data faster and create less of a bottleneck.

text:
It's been common practice for over a decade to test graphics cards with a very fast CPU so that the CPU is not the bottleneck.
It is highly unusual for a graphics card to fall over itself like the B580 did, for instance, the 4060 lost about 2% performance in Spider-Man between the 9800X3D and 5700X3D, whereas the B580 lost 32%. If HUB had tested a Radeon card, it would almost certainly have scaled similarly to the GeForce.
So the B580 behavior was unexpected, and it was only unearthed because Hardware Canucks was trying to investigate the impact of ReBar (which is not the sole culprit here).
There are too many combinations of CPU + GPU for reviewers to test every single one, even if sites were trying to limit configurations to "common" or "popular" setups, so standardizing on a high end CPU for GPU tests allows for a common frame of reference. Normally, you can extrapolate relative performance of cards based on this testing practice, but the intel Arc and Battlemage cards are outliers in this respect.

text:
In CPU intensive games, the two main factors that make the RTX 4060 perform better than the Intel Arc B580 are:

1. Larger L2 Cache:

When there is more L2 cache, there is faster access to data, and the latency or delay between the processor and the GPU is reduced. This is crucial in CPU intensive games, as the CPU needs to access more data, and a larger cache can speed up these processes.

2. Lower Bandwidth and Reduced CPU Load:

When the GPU has lower bandwidth, the CPU has less strain to handle. In this case, the GPU requires less bandwidth, allowing the CPU to access data more quickly. This helps reduce the CPU bottleneck and results in better performance in games that are more dependent on the CPU.

As a result, these two factors make the RTX 4060 perform better in CPU intensive games compared to the Intel Arc B580, because the lower bandwidth and larger cache help the CPU process data faster and create less of a bottleneck.
